summary: All 6 in-scope items implemented and every gate is green. (A) Duel horizontal jitter: extracted a shared DuelStackShell (parallel to FreeStackShell) that owns the Navbar + tab band + width-matched content container, pinned to ONE canonical width constant DUEL_STACK_WIDTH=max-w-4xl used by both /duel and /duel/leaderboard, so the band and content left-edges are identical on both routes and can never drift again. This also deleted a duplicated DuelTab component (leaderboard) and a duplicated band in DuelHome. (B) Free-stack vertical jitter: removed the `!gameSection && <Navbar>` guard in FreeStackShell so the navbar renders on Leaderboard/Play/Daily alike, pinning the tab band at the same top on all three; ClimbScene's touch `fixed inset-0` fullscreen path is untouched and no transform was added to the game wrapper. (C) Doubled 'climb': extracted pure helper climbEyebrowLabel() that appends ' climb' only when the label doesn't already contain the whole word (case-insensitive), so 'Free climb'->'Free climb' (was 'FREE CLIMB CLIMB'), 'Daily'->'Daily climb', 'Tech'->'Tech climb'. (D) Mobile navbar: removed the baked-in `inline-flex` from the GHOST link base (it beat the appended `hidden` at equal specificity, leaking the 1v1/Daily/Free climb links under the wordmark below sm) and restructured the breadcrumb into a min-w-0 chain with a truncate label so wordmark+breadcrumb can't overflow/overlap the auth buttons at 375px. (E) /play desktop stage: laid the how-to/controls card beside the canvas in a max-w-5xl lg-row instead of stacking it under a lonely 9:16 strip; the aspect-locked canvas is NOT resized (conservative, per guardrail — shared ClimbScene + leaderboard fairness), only ClimbPlayClient's /play-specific PlayShell layout changed, and touch fullscreen is unaffected (lg: breakpoint + ClimbScene fixed path). (F) /climb header: changed the visible H1 from 'Free climb leaderboard' to 'Global leaderboard'; navbar breadcrumb ('Free climb') + eyebrow ('Free climb · no payment') still carry the phrase (now 2x, not 3x) and the <title> metadata keeps the full phrase for SEO. Added 2 unit-test files (climbEyebrow, navbarResponsive), both proven fail-first. Test count 786->794 (86->88 files); no route-mode flips.

designDecisions: A: chose full DuelStackShell extraction over a shared-width-constant-only fix because the band + a DuelTab were genuinely duplicated across the two routes; a shell guarantees the band never diverges (mirrors FreeStackShell) and still exposes DUEL_STACK_WIDTH as the single source of truth. Kept the extraction presentational-only: all DuelHome state/logic stays inside `children`, so blast radius on the large client component is limited to the outer wrapper markup. Picked max-w-4xl (DuelHome's existing width, fits its 2-col grid) so the busier page doesn't move; only the leaderboard widened 2xl->4xl.

E: deliberately did NOT widen the live canvas. ClimbScene is shared by /duel replays, GameOverlay (landing), and DailyClimbClient, and its 9:16 lock keeps visible-world constant for leaderboard fairness (useCanvasSize ASPECT lock). Widening the canvas column to a definite `lg:flex-1` (not shrink-to-fit) avoids reintroducing the canvas measurement feedback loop the hook warns about. Tradeoff: the canvas stays a strip; the win is the how-to card now fills the horizontal space beside it rather than the whole surface being a thin centered column.

learnings.insight: Cross-route chrome jitter came from each route sizing the shared band from its own content width (duel: max-w-4xl vs max-w-2xl → 112px horizontal shift; free-stack: navbar present on LB only → 56px vertical shift). The durable fix is a shared shell that owns the chrome at ONE pinned width/structure, independent of per-page content — not per-page width tweaks that drift again. Both stacks now do this (FreeStackShell, new DuelStackShell) via a single width constant.
learnings.action: When a nav band 'jumps' between sibling routes, look for the band being rendered per-page (duplicated) and unify it into a shared shell with a pinned width constant, rather than matching widths by hand on each page.

learnings.insight: `inline-flex` and `hidden` are both single-class display utilities at EQUAL specificity, so combining a base `inline-flex` with `hidden sm:inline-flex` is decided by stylesheet source order, not className order — Tailwind emitted inline-flex after hidden, so the element stayed visible on mobile. Never bake a `display` utility into a shared base class that callers then try to override with `hidden`; let each caller own its responsive display.
learnings.action: reviewer: flag any shared class constant that hardcodes inline-flex/flex/block/grid when call sites append `hidden`/`sm:*` display variants — it's a same-specificity conflict that silently loses.

learnings.insight: useCanvasSize (app/src/hooks/useCanvasSize.ts) reads the canvas wrapper's PARENT clientWidth to stay out of its own width feedback loop. If you place ClimbScene in a shrink-to-fit flex item (e.g. `lg:shrink-0` with no basis), the parent width becomes content-driven by the canvas and the loop returns. When adding a two-column play layout, give the canvas column a DEFINITE width (`lg:flex-1` or an explicit width), never content-sizing.
learnings.action: Any layout change around ClimbScene must keep the canvas's ancestor width independent of the canvas (definite, not content-driven), or the 9:16 sizing can oscillate.

learnings.insight: The doubled 'climb' eyebrow came from a template `[ {label} climb ]` fed labels that sometimes already contain the word ('Free climb') and sometimes don't ('Daily','Tech'). The fix is a whole-word conditional-append helper (climbEyebrowLabel), unit-tested against the exact production caller labels (ClimbPlayClient 'Free climb', DailyClimbClient 'Daily', GameOverlay category labels). Deleting the word would have broken Daily/Tech.
learnings.action: For any 'label + fixed word' template, check every caller's label before assuming the word is absent; prefer a tested helper over editing the template inline.
